raw_response:
Here is my management plan for this year.

---

I am 70 years old now, and I have been farming this same land for 50 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the extension leaflets and I understand what the agricultural station people say when they come to the village. But to be honest, most of what I know comes from doing it myself and from watching my neighbors — Old Zhao on the east side and Old Liu on the west. My son and daughter-in-law both work in a factory in Handan, so it is mostly me and my wife handling the farm day to day. My grandson helps when he is home from school. My son sends some money back every month, but I do not like to use that for farm inputs — that is for the boy's school fees and for emergencies. The farm has to pay for itself.

I have 5 mu, all wheat-maize double cropping. That is what this soil has always done, and I am not about to change it now. The soil is loamy and pretty good, but it gets tired after the corn, so you have to feed it. I remember 2013 when I tried to cut back on fertilizer to save money for my wife's medical bills. The wheat was so short and thin I lost almost a third of my yield. I learned that lesson. But I also do not throw money away like some of the young people with big farms.

For the winter wheat, I plant in mid-October, right after the maize comes off. I use an improved variety — I save most of my own seed but I buy a little new seed from the county supply store every couple of years to keep it strong. The extension people say 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I have found that if I put down about 16 kg total — some as compound fertilizer at planting and some urea at jointing — I get a decent stand without wasting money. I spread about 25 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting and work it in with the rotary tiller. Then in March, when the wheat is at jointing, I topdress with about 20 kg of urea per mu if the wheat looks a little yellow. If it is already dark green, I might cut that back to 15 kg. That saves a bit, and at 70 I have learned that more is not always better.

I irrigate the wheat three times — once after planting to help it germinate before winter, once at green-up in spring if the rain is not enough, and once at jointing. I have a well, but the electricity for the pump keeps getting more expensive, so I do not waste water. Three times is usually enough if the spring is normal. For weeds, I spray herbicide once in early spring. I do not use insecticide on wheat — never had a big enough problem to justify the cost.

For the summer maize, the window is so tight. Sometimes we cut the wheat on June 6th and I have to plant the corn by June 8th or the growing season is too short. I put all the fertilizer in at planting — about 20 kg of compound fertilizer and 8 kg of urea per mu, right in the seed furrow. There is no time to come back for a second application, and the summer rains usually help carry it through. I buy hybrid seed every year — you cannot save hybrid seed, it does not breed true. I learned that the hard way in the 1990s. It costs about 45 yuan per mu, which is a lot, but it pays back.

I irrigate the maize once or twice depending on the summer rains. Last July we had good rain and I only irrigated once. If August turns dry, I will pump a second time. I spray herbicide once and insecticide once in July because the armyworms have been worse the last few years.

At 70, my back is not what it used to be. I do most of the spreading, irrigating, and spraying myself, and my wife helps. But I hire Old Wang's son for one day at wheat harvest and one day at maize planting — he has a small combine and a planter, and it saves my back. That is 150 yuan per day, so 300 yuan total for hired labor, but at my age it is worth it. My wife and I handle everything else.

I expect about 400 kg per mu of wheat and 450 kg per mu of maize if the weather is normal. Last year was okay — not great, not terrible. I am not trying to break records. I just need enough grain for my family, some to sell, and to not lose money on this little plot. My total input costs this year will be around 1,350 yuan. That is a big chunk of cash for a 5-mu farm, but if I skimp now, I will regret it at harvest.
